title: Titanium Compressor Blade
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (Grade 5, UNS R56400) was selected for this engine component application because its 900+ MPa tensile enables thin-wall lightweighting under cyclic loading. The alpha-beta microstructure provides 45% higher specific strength than 4140 steel, critical for weight-sensitive designs. Its 6.7 W/mK thermal conductivity simplifies thermal management. This rationale is driven by axial compressor rotor blade and service environment demands.
process: 5-axis CNC roughing for engine component geometry
Wire EDM contour profiling with Class 6g gauge
CMM per AS9102 with Class 6g gauge
surfaceTreatment: Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service
commonFailures: SCC in chloride-rich marine atmosphere - controlled by bake-out 300C + corrosion-inhibiting primer

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Compressor Blade suitable for Axial compressor rotor blade?
faq.a: Titanium Compressor Blade uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address engine component operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Compressor Blade?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Compressor Blade require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. engine component components receive Shot peening Almen 0.008-0.012A inducing compressive residual stress for extended HCF life in aerospace service. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Compressor Blade shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Compressor blade / Rotor blade engine component components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
